findings_not_breaks: refusal, not coherence: any program needing a second name for a block kosh — even a safe, in-block, read-only alias that never outlives the block — is refused; safety is bought by narrowing what can be written
waste counts against the budget: a parimita budget of N bytes holds roughly N/2 bytes of live kosh data after growth (192 reported for 72 live at cap 4)
the exhaustion error names nothing: 'kshetra purnam' gives no line and no count, unlike E_PARIMITA (which names the block's line)
the benefit is real (Claude's kb1, cited): 100,000 blocks, each a 100-number kosh: 0 KB, 0.02 s on the branch, against v289's 400 MB, 0.46-0.59 s
ws1_attack.outlives_block: refused at COMPILE time on the branch, for every shape tried (visible alias, call-mediated alias, container stores, function return); no post-block read can happen
ws1_attack.parimana_in_use: meaningful — counts every arena slot, live and wasted, 16-byte aligned (kosh grown 1 -> 2 -> 4 reports 48 -> 112 -> 192; the 1000-push case reports exactly 16896, the sum of all eleven slots caps 1..1024, verified to the byte); drops to 0 at block exit (the arena is freed)
ws1_attack.verdict: the program that breaks it was not found — the branch closes the holes it claims to close, and its failure mode on exhaustion is a clean error, not a crash
